Why can sound not travel through vacuum?
questions.a: Sound travels as particles of the medium vibrating; with no particles in vacuum there is nothing to vibrate.

questions.q: Through which medium does sound travel fastest - solid, liquid or gas?
questions.a: Solids, because their particles are closest, passing the vibration on fastest.

questions.q: Why do astronauts on the moon use radios to talk?
questions.a: The moon has no atmosphere (vacuum), so sound cannot carry between them.

questions.q: What kind of wave is sound - longitudinal or transverse?
questions.a: Longitudinal - the particles vibrate along the direction the wave travels, forming compressions and rarefactions.

questions.q: Define compressions and rarefactions.
questions.a: Compressions are regions where particles crowd together (high pressure); rarefactions are where they spread apart (low pressure).

questions.q: Why is sound called a mechanical wave?
questions.a: It needs a material medium whose particles vibrate to carry the energy from place to place.
